name: Sporobolus

project_scope.note: Current manifest contains all three canonical species. S. compositus species-rank card is PASS (Hays, Bexar, Kerr), while disputed variety-level/Travis records are excluded from that determination. Historical B149 HOLD text below is retained as historical context, not current admission status.

priority: upper sheath with or without hidden cleistogenes
glume roughness and fertile lemma hairs
mature spikelet and grain when perennial species overlap
study_strategy.warning: Panicle contraction and plant height overlap with age, drought and mowing. Species-rank S. compositus is now canonical; its disputed variety-level records must not be silently treated as resolved.

quick_split: S. clandestinus — perennial rough dropseed with contracted panicle.
S. vaginiflorus — small annual poverty dropseed with cleistogamous flowers hidden in upper sheaths.
S. compositus — robust perennial complex retained as HOLD pending cleaner local county/specimen resolution.

fast_fill_note: Sporobolus clandestinus and S. vaginiflorus each now have an exact-species public-domain diagnostic reference. Both remain presentation-source-limited pending easy rights-clear field photos; scientific status is unchanged.

source_concept_status.note: Current canonical species.json: Hays, Bexar, Kerr PASS at species rank; historical variety-level/Travis dispute remains excluded.

look_here_first: 1. Inspect the plant base: annual roots or a persistent perennial tuft? 2. Examine the whole panicle: tightly contracted versus longer and more open. 3. At a node, lift the upper leaf sheath gently to look for hidden self-pollinating spikelets (cleistogenes). 4. Magnify a mature spikelet: glume surface, lemma hairs and fruit are more reliable than fall color.

shared_structure_examples.plain_english: The branching flower/seed head at the top of the grass.
shared_structure_examples.look_for: Branch length, angle and how closely the spikelets crowd the axis.
shared_structure_examples.why_it_matters: Separates the short contracted heads of poverty/rough dropseed from the often longer compositus head; head openness overlaps.

shared_structure_examples.plain_english: Tiny flowering unit, outer bracts and bract around its flower.
shared_structure_examples.look_for: Detach a mature spikelet and examine outer glumes and lemma under magnification.
shared_structure_examples.why_it_matters: Roughness and hairs help separate perennial species; requires actual macro, not habit photo.

shared_structure_examples.plain_english: The leaf tube around the stem; some hidden self-pollinating flowers develop inside.
shared_structure_examples.look_for: Upper sheaths of S. vaginiflorus; document a concealed spikelet without tearing away its point of origin.
shared_structure_examples.why_it_matters: Especially useful confirmation of annual poverty dropseed.

shared_structure_examples.plain_english: The lower grass stem and persistent tuft or annual root system.
shared_structure_examples.look_for: Whether old perennial tillers persist at the crown or an annual plant roots from a single season.
shared_structure_examples.why_it_matters: First division between S. vaginiflorus and the two perennial species.

genus_diagnostics.genus_recognition: Grasses with small spikelets in a panicle and dropseed-type grains. Recognize grass anatomy first: culm nodes, sheath, ligule and spikelets; no single panicle silhouette confirms genus.

confusable_genera.distinction: Also fine-panicled grasses; dissect spikelet glumes/lemmas and mature fruit rather than relying on cloudlike heads.
Usually multiple florets per spikelet; compare an entire dissected spikelet against Sporobolus, where spikelets are generally one-flowered.
